Agony derives from Greek agon contest or struggle, rather than the source -gony generation suffix. Agony is from Greek agonia contest or struggle, derived from agon, and does not contain the Greek -gony production/reproduction suffix. The similar letters are coincidental across the actual historical boundary.

Apprehensive derives through apprehens-, the participial stem of Latin apprehendere grasp, and extended mental/fearful meanings. HENS is explicitly listed by CUNY as same-family participial form of HEND.
Reprehensible derives from Latin reprehensibilis, from reprehendere seize or blame; -hens- participial variant is a documented morpheme, within prehens.
